assumptions.scope: Readable NUL-terminated input; first NUL and length result.
assumptions.justification: Architecture implementation is external to the annotated translation unit; WP reasons from this contract.

assumptions.scope: Readable source, writable disjoint destination for len bytes; exact copy and return pointer.
assumptions.justification: Models the external memcpy called after frontend builtin substitution.

assumptions.scope: Profile-specific exceptional control flow only.
assumptions.justification: Existing terminates/exits/ensures combination and CONFIG_BUG effects require review before a complete proof claim.

assumptions.scope: x86 front-end compatibility only; no inheritance to another architecture.
assumptions.justification: Existing shims adapt assembly traps and C23 inference; equivalence is not established by function-body identity.

assumptions.scope: GNU preprocessing, typeof, int128 and builtin spellings.
assumptions.justification: Each command-line substitution must be bound to source/configuration identity and checked for its target use.

assumptions.scope: count readable bytes required when count > 0.
assumptions.justification: This accepted domain can be narrower than an API use which encounters a terminator before count; no caller proof claimed.

assumptions.scope: 64-bit limbs; positive usize and shift count within documented bounds.
assumptions.justification: Standalone harness supplies the kernel types; body gate and profile calibration are separate requirements.

assumptions.scope: Fixed 64-bit unsigned/signed arithmetic; int field positions and widths.
assumptions.justification: Harness uses long long typedefs; original kernel type identity and supported constructs require review.

assumptions.scope: Enum/constants/macros and logging replacement used by five copied leaves.
assumptions.justification: Must be checked against pinned insn headers and original configuration.

assumptions.scope: Non-returning BUG branches in the standalone instruction harness.
assumptions.justification: Historical report leaves termination obligations unresolved; keep these dependencies visible.

assumptions.scope: Unconstrained pure classifier result.
assumptions.justification: Current stub does not specify the actual ADRP encoding relation; stronger functional properties need that relation.

assumptions.scope: Eight bounded valid-input ARM32 safety-search entries; no production caller coverage or universal API proof.
assumptions.justification: Local objects and bounded counts expose candidate operations to Eva without encoding an expected implementation result.

assumptions.scope: Configured ARMv7 whole-TU preprocessing with genuine ARM headers and the closed common GNU token shims; ARM inline assembly semantics remain unsupported.
assumptions.justification: The route preserves the real compile command and excludes x86 header overrides, but parsing and the unreachable declaration do not model ARM assembly.

assumptions.scope: A 256-byte readable zero table establishes only index safety for strncasecmp; it does not model Linux case folding.
assumptions.justification: The first RTE/Eva scan is for invalid operations. Functional comparison claims require a separately source-gated lib/ctype.c table.

assumptions.scope: Exact byte-copy semantics used when Frama-C lowers packed unaligned reads; no proof of the ARM assembly memcpy implementation.
assumptions.justification: Without the explicit Eva builtin, generated default assigns leave packed read results uninitialized and create tool-model alarms unrelated to the selected kernel body.

assumptions.scope: Normal entirely mapped little-endian ARM32 four-byte load only; excludes the exception-table fixup, page crossing, emitted instructions and concurrent mapping changes.
assumptions.justification: Frama-C cannot interpret the ARM inline assembly output. The packed C load preserves byte semantics for the bounded in-object string drivers while keeping the unsupported boundary behaviour outside every claim.

assumptions.scope: Sequential conventional strchr result for a readable NUL-terminated string; excludes verification of arch/arm/lib/strchr.S, timing and concurrent mutation.
assumptions.justification: The selected generic strsep body reaches generic strpbrk, which calls the external ARM assembly strchr implementation. The bounded C dependency model prevents an arbitrary-pointer default result from masquerading as a strsep defect.

assumptions.scope: Per-candidate domains derived before body review from public declarations and non-candidate caller sites; the first PCI pass is bounded below 2 GiB and is not universal caller coverage.
assumptions.justification: Analyzer-first drivers must make pointers and scalar relationships meaningful without importing expectations from the candidate implementation. Boundary and functional passes remain separate follow-up evidence.

assumptions.scope: Direct pinned ARM32 translation-unit analysis using its retained configured compile command and genuine headers; inline assembly and unmodeled external functions remain unsupported and visible.
assumptions.justification: The new route removes hand-copied candidate bodies. Closed GNU token shims permit parsing but do not supply semantics for ARM assembly, MMIO, atomics or external dependencies.

assumptions.scope: Only the direct bios32.c ARM32 search target. Scalar inferred temporaries retain single evaluation and operand type. GCC-enforced constant checks in unrelated inline helpers are suppressed; unrelated MM padding becomes a fixed non-flexible aligned member; an unused kernfs lock-array declaration takes its UP size. No MM/kernfs layout, array-expression, cacheline or compile-time-diagnostic claim is accepted.
assumptions.justification: Frama-C 33 otherwise stops before pcibios_align_resource() on inferred-auto syntax, Linux's sizeof(void) constant detector, non-final nested zero-length padding, and an unevaluated runtime ilog2 branch in a kernfs array bound. The configured object already passed GCC compilation. Each wrapper includes the pinned header, is target-opt-in, and adapts constructs outside the selected function so the unchanged candidate can reach raw Eva analysis.

assumptions.scope: Token-identical selected function under the configured ARM32 machdep with a minimal declaration environment. This establishes neither whole-translation-unit parsing nor behavior of omitted headers, inline helpers, assembly, attributes or unselected functions.
assumptions.justification: The retained direct bios32.c attempts stop in unrelated transitive headers before candidate analysis. Function provenance still rejects any changed named declarator, parameter list or body token; narrowing the surrounding declarations permits analyzer-first triage without rewriting the candidate.

assumptions.scope: First bounded RTE/Eva pass only. Host lookup returns one valid modeled bridge; default and optional bridge alignment callbacks return the candidate start. No functional result, real PCI topology, callback implementation or concurrent mutation claim is accepted.
assumptions.justification: The selected ARM function delegates through these interfaces. Valid deterministic implementations prevent unrelated arbitrary-pointer defaults from masquerading as candidate defects while leaving the candidate's own accesses and arithmetic visible.

assumptions.scope: Bounded ARM module image with eleven section headers, bounded relocation counts, valid temporary-image addresses and known section-name offsets. One SHT_REL sh_info retains its full untrusted 32-bit range because the generic loader has not range-checked it before this architecture hook. It is not universal malformed-ELF, allocation, or functional coverage.
assumptions.justification: The real caller validates the ELF header, section table, section-name offsets and contents before invoking the architecture hook, but its first sh_info range check occurs later in apply_relocations(). Preserving that caller-permitted field exposes candidate indexing instead of assuming the safety condition under investigation.

assumptions.scope: Token-identical candidate under the retained little-endian ARMv7 ABI and multi_v7 configuration, with only the directly used ELF/module declarations and constants. It proves neither whole-translation-unit parsing nor omitted kernel layout and header behavior.
assumptions.justification: The source gate prevents candidate rewriting while the compact declaration environment bypasses unrelated Linux header constructs unsupported by Frama-C. Exact declarations, configuration values and ABI widths are checked by a compile-only gate against the pinned configured kernel headers.

assumptions.scope: First candidate-orchestrator RTE/Eva pass only. String comparison and init-prefix classification execute concrete C; relocation sorting is inert and count_plts returns any value from zero through the relocation count. DYNAMIC_FTRACE is disabled, so fixed_plts has zero entries. No relocation-counting, sorting, PLT-content, or functional-result claim is accepted.
assumptions.justification: The April 2026 candidate orchestrates these helpers. Conservative bounded return values expose its own pointer/index/size arithmetic while postponing source-identical helper analysis to a separate dependency pass. The confirmed access occurs before their results can affect control flow, and the exact kernel QEMU witness independently reproduces it.

assumptions.scope: First broad fake-pass RTE/Eva scan of one instruction backed by two readable successors, with every 8-bit opcode, external BPF registers 0 through 10, a full 32-bit immediate, verifier-valid MOVSX offsets 8, 16 and 32, one in-range conditional branch and no output buffer. Invalid encodings may be rejected by the candidate. This is not full verifier-state, internal AX-register, live emission-buffer, branch-target, helper-call or functional JIT coverage.
assumptions.justification: build_body() passes verifier-approved instructions to build_insn() first with target == NULL. The bounded driver keeps direct object accesses meaningful without encoding an expected return value or native instruction sequence before analyzer triage.

assumptions.scope: Token-identical build_insn() named declarator and body under the retained little-endian 32-bit ARM machdep, with a compact declaration environment. Only the static declaration prefix is removed so the separate driver can call the candidate; the source gate records that difference. The compact bpf_prog has three instructions for this first-pass model and is not a complete kernel layout claim.
assumptions.justification: Eleven exact whole-translation-unit attempts stopped in unrelated transitive headers before candidate analysis. Function provenance rejects changes to parameters or body while the slice bypasses those frontend-only failures and preserves the analyzer-first candidate.

assumptions.scope: Initial analyzer-isolation pass only. Instruction emitters and register-transfer helpers are inert C definitions, so no generated-A32 value, instruction count, helper implementation or output-buffer safety claim is accepted. Direct operations in build_insn() remain visible; dependency bodies and live target-buffer properties require subsequent source-gated passes.
assumptions.justification: The first retained result preceded candidate-body diagnosis. Explicitly incomplete dependencies separated direct candidate alarms from a large helper closure; every surviving lead must be rerun with the relevant genuine helper before classification as a kernel defect.
